(i) the minimum standard deviation of a molecular population decreases with the quart root of its mean, and (ii) the minimum variance is inversely proportional to a parameter called the ‘information rate’, which is the ratio of the number of molecules that are signalling in a control loop to the number of molecules in the system.

(i) the minimum achievable standard deviation in abundancies is bounded by the quartic root (1/4) of the number of signaling events and that (ii) cells increase the number of signaling event by several orders of magnitude in order to reduce the standard deviation of molecular abundances.

the fundamental limit to noise reduction in biological systems is set by the stochastic nature of chemical reactions, and the only way around this fundamental limit is to increase the number of chemical reactions, which is the strategy adopted by biological systems.

the fundamental limits on molecular fluctuations are severe and that the biological systems have evolved strategies to circumvent these limits.

there is a fundamental limit on the ability of negative feedback to suppress the fluctuations of individual molecular species in a cell.

it is not possible to achieve high precision in the control of molecular numbers.
